text: Search now happens in two places at once: Google's results pages and the AI-generated answers inside ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google's own AI Overviews. And winning only one of them leaves real traffic and brand visibility on the table. Because a page built purely to rank in organic search won’t necessarily get pulled into an AI-generated answer (and vice versa). In this guide, you'll learn what AEO (answer engine optimization) and SEO (search engine optimization) are, how they differ, where they overlap, and how to succeed with both. AEO vs SEO: what are the core differences? At the simplest level, AEO is about being included in AI-generated answers while SEO is about ranking in search engines. But the two overlap. Many of the same signals that help you rank in Google also increase your chances of being cited by AI tools. And AI features, like Google AI Mode , live in both worlds. Here's how AEO and SEO differ — and the similarities they share: AEO SEO Goal Get your content cited or mentioned in AI-generated answers (and in voice search) to grow brand awareness and drive traffic to your site. Rank high in organic search — including search engine results pages (SERPs) and AI-powered features like AI Overviews — to drive traffic to your site. User behavior Users ask questions and read or listen to the AI-generated answer. They might also explore the sources used to create the AI response (citations). Users browse SERPs and decide which link to click. They also explore AI-generated answers to satisfy their search intent and potentially click to learn more. User intent Get detailed information directly from the AI search engine. Navigate to a site for detailed information or get an instant response via a SERP feature . Discovery surface AI answers, citations, embedded URLs, brand mentions, and Google's AI features. Direct links, featured snippets, People Also Ask, local packs, knowledge panels, AI Overviews, and AI Mode. Success metric Increase in AI brand mentions , citations, or placements in AI-generated responses. Higher rankings and visibility across both search results and AI-powered features, leading to more organic traffic. Let’s go over what AEO and SEO are in greater detail. What is AEO? AEO (answer engine optimization) is a digital marketing strategy that helps make your web content easily discoverable by AI search engines like ChatGPT and voice assistants like Alexa. The goal of an AEO strategy is to have your content appear or be cited when someone asks AI a question related to your business, product, service, or industry. Because with 77% of ChatGPT users in the USA treating it like a search engine, and nearly 60% of consumers using AI tools to shop, AEO can drive discovery, trust, and conversions. For example, if you sell a project management tool for finance teams, you want your brand to appear when someone asks ChatGPT, " What's the best project management software for finance teams? " What is SEO? SEO (search engine optimization) is a digital marketing strategy that helps your website rank higher in search engine results like Google and Bing. SEO focuses on keywords, backlinks , content depth, and site structure to drive organic traffic and improve your visibility in the SERPs. At the same time, SEO strategies continually evolve to include SERP features like AI Overviews , carousels, featured snippets, People Also A sk boxes, knowledge panels, and more. How AEO and SEO work together AEO and SEO work together by making your content findable, authoritative, and quotable. SEO builds your domain authority and ensures your content is trustworthy, while AEO ensures that content is easier for AI systems to parse, understand, and cite. So, does ranking well on Google get you cited by AI? Partly. When we compared AI answers with Google's organic results, our research found: AI favors trusted domains : Strong organic rankings and authority make a domain more likely to be cited AI doesn't necessarily cite high-ranking pages : AI often pulls deeper subpages, blog posts, or documentation within trusted domains instead of the exact ranking URLs Overlap depends on the platform : Google AI Mode's sidebar shows lower overlap with Google's top 10, while its additional links have much higher overlap. Perplexity has the strongest alignment with Google, and ChatGPT the weakest, though it still leans on authoritative domains. Authority drives inclusion : AI consistently prioritizes domains with strong backlinks, authority, and visibility — even when it pulls different pages than Google's top results In short, AEO extends SEO rather than competing with it: the same fundamentals that earn a domain trust in Google's eyes are what make it worth citing in an AI-generated answer. How to succeed in both AEO and SEO There are many strategies to help you succeed in both AEO and SEO — from creating original content to building external signals and structuring your content for retrieval. Let's break those down in detail. 1. Create unique, research-backed content Creating unique, research-backed content sends positive signals to search engines and AI search platforms, as both reward content grounded in real experience that AI alone can't generate. So when planning your digital content, make sure you bring something original to the table — like personal experience, fresh data, or expert insights. For example, we conducted original research on whether backlinks still matter for AI. That post is one of the first results in organic search. The post also appears in AI Overviews. And is cited in AI search platforms like ChatGPT. To create content that boosts both SEO and AEO: Write from first-hand experience: Share what you've actually done, tested, or figured out through real work. Even small insights can help your content stand out. Use original data: Run surveys, document experiments, or pull insights from your own product. Unique stats and internal findings add credibility and increase the chances of being cited. Add author bios: Make it clear who's behind the content and why they're worth listening to. Mention each author's role, area of expertise, or hands-on experience. Quote experts: If you don't have direct experience, speak to someone who does. Bring in their insights, ideas, or frameworks. It adds depth and signals trust to both AI and human readers. 2. Build authority through brand mentions and backlinks Building authority through brand mentions and backlinks matters because search engines and AI search platforms favor sources that other trusted sites reference. In practice, this translates into attracting: Backlinks (links from other relevant websites that point to your content): Backlinks remain one of the core SEO ranking factors, and our research on the impact of backlinks for AI search found that they’re also associated with greater visibility in AI search Brand mentions (linked and unlinked mentions to your brand across trusted sites): Brand mentions are especially important for AI search platforms, which often rely on recognizable brands when generating answers As Alex Birkett noted in our webinar, both signals are critical if you want to succeed in SEO and AEO: Do backlinks still matter? Yeah, a hundred percent. They’re still an input vector for your website’s authority and page authority, and they’re important in both classic and LLM optimization. But brand mentions also play a big role — even unlinked ones — because with LLMs it’s more text-based: the model looks at the text around the prompt and whether your brand is mentioned there. What matters is being referenced across multiple trusted sources. Alex Birkett, Co-Founder of Omniscient Digital Here are a few tips that can help you earn more mentions and backlinks: Create content backed by original research and expert insights that others want to reference and link to Contribute expert commentary to blogs or media outlets in your niche Pitch guest posts to sites with high authority and strong reputation in your industry Work with writers who regularly contribute to credible publications and already have relationships with editors Collaborate with trusted brands or creators on co-branded content, original studies, or interviews that naturally lead to mentions and links For example, HubSpot frequently publishes original, expertise-driven content, like its annual State of Marketing Report , which features original research and essential industry data. The report's page has generated thousands of backlinks over the years: It also gets mentioned by various bloggers, outlets, and other relevant industry players: Creating this kind of content consistently has paid off in both channels: HubSpot has an extremely high AI visibility score , is frequently cited by AI search platforms, and draws millions of organic visits each month. 3. Use entities to strengthen topic relevance Using entities — clearly named concepts like people, companies, products, or places — strengthens topical relevance by helping search engines and AI match your page to relevant topics and queries. Google uses these entities as part of its Knowledge Graph — a database of facts about people, companies, products, and places. And AI search platforms like ChatGPT rely on consistent entity signals to make connections between prompts, topics, and brands. For example, writing about Amazon could mean the company or the rainforest. Adding terms like "Amazon Prime," "Jeff Bezos," or "ecommerce" makes it clear you're talking about the business. To effectively use entities in your content: Use consistent terminology for tools, frameworks, and products : Say "Google AI Overviews" every time instead of switching to "AIOs" or "Google AIOs" Include your brand and product names clearly : Place them near key points of value so search engines and AI systems connect your brand to what you offer Add related concepts and subtopics : If you're writing about Tesla, mention "electric vehicles," "Model 3," or "EV charging stations," and cover themes like pricing and safety Use examples and analogies that reinforce the topic : Comparing website architecture to a house blueprint works because both determine how easily people can find their way around For example: Could be better (inconsistent and generic) Good (entities, consistency, and clarity) "Our tool tracks rankings in Google SERPs and AIOs, plus AI mode and chatbots. You can also see which sources mention your site so you know where you're cited." "Our platform tracks rankings in Google SERPs and Google AI Overviews, plus visibility in Google AI Mode and ChatGPT. You can also see the citation sources used for your pages (e.g., Reddit, YouTube, G2), so you know where you're being referenced." 4. Structure your content for clarity Structuring your content for clarity helps search engines and AI search platforms understand relationships between concepts and determine what's most important on your page. In practice, this means leading each section with a concise, standalone answer before adding supporting detail, and organizing the rest of your content in a logical, hierarchical way with clear sections and formatting. To optimize your content structure for SEO and AEO (and users): Use clear hierarchical heading structure (H1, H2, H3) that creates logical topic relationships Place key information in strategic locations like the beginnings of paragraphs, sections, and documents Use ordered lists for processes/rankings and bulleted lists for related items Add structured data markup (schema.org) when possible to explicitly label content types like FAQs, products, or reviews Maintain consistent formatting throughout your content to reinforce structure For example, this Semrush article uses clear H2s and answers each heading's question in the first sentence of the section. It also breaks related items into bullet points, making the page easier for readers to scan and for bots to parse. It also uses numbered lists to outline steps and keeps formatting consistent, making complex information easier to follow. 5. Keep your content fresh Keeping your content fresh requires regular audits, as search engines and AI systems prefer citing up-to-date content. Fresh content is an important SEO ranking factor and is key to content quality, especially for pages where relevance changes quickly (e.g., news). Research also shows that AI search platforms have a clear preference for pages that are recent and trustworthy. That preference makes sense given how AI answers are built. Many of these platforms pull from live retrieval systems, so when two pages cover the same ground, the more recently updated one is more likely to get cited. Updating the publish date alone doesn't help — the content itself needs genuinely new information, current examples, or corrected details for that recency signal to mean anything. Here's what you can do to keep your content fresh and relevant: Update factual information, statistics, and examples with the most current data Refresh screenshots and visuals to reflect current interfaces and designs Add new sections covering recent developments in your topic area Remove or update references to outdated tools, methods, or practices Optimize for emerging keywords and changing search intent (the goal behind a search query) 6. Make your content extractable for AI answers Making your content extractable for AI answers means structuring each section so AI systems can pull it into an answer on its own, since they use specific passages rather than entire pages. To make your content easier for AI systems to lift and cite directly: Lead with a short, direct answer . Keep the first sentence of any section you want cited under roughly 40 words, and make it a complete, standalone answer — free of pronouns or references that only make sense alongside the rest of the paragraph. Use FAQ-style Q&A formatting for predictable follow-up questions . A heading phrased as a question, followed immediately by a direct answer, is easier for an AI system to match to a user's prompt than a heading like "Additional Considerations." Keep entity names consistent throughout a section . Switching between "Google AI Overviews," "AIOs," and "Google's AI feature" to describe the same thing makes it harder for AI systems to treat your mentions as references to the same entity. Semrush's Content Optimizer analyzes content for extractability signals like these and surfaces specific fixes. It works on existing pages too, so you can enter a URL and see what an older article needs. How to monitor AEO and SEO To monitor AEO and SEO, track your keyword rankings and AI prompt visibility side by side with tools like Semrush's SEO Toolkit and AI Visibility Toolkit . Using these tools regularly helps you understand what works (and what doesn't) so you can make strategic improvements. Key metrics to analyze include: Keyword rankings in organic search results Visibility in Google's AI features like AI Overviews and AI Mode AI Brand Mentions and rankings across AI search platforms Citation sources linking to your content AI Share of Voice against competitors for your priority topics Competitor performance across both channels For example, you can use our Keyword Magic Tool to find keywords to rank on Google — whether on SERPs or in AI features. For the AEO side, Prompt Research surfaces the prompts people ask AI platforms about your topic, so you know which questions to target before you write. You can then track the keywords you found in Position Tracking to monitor your Google rankings. For AI search, add your priority prompts to Prompt Tracking. It shows whether AI platforms cite, recommend, or ignore your brand for each prompt, so you can watch your AI visibility move the same way you'd watch your keyword rankings. Finally, use the AI Visibility Toolkit's Narrative Drivers report to see the specific AI prompts where you appear (or don't) versus competitors across AI Mode, ChatGPT, Gemini, and other platforms. By tracking both SEO and AEO side by side, you'll see where traffic is slipping and where AI is picking it up — so you can double down on the channels that drive results. Frequently asked questions about AEO vs SEO Will AEO replace SEO? AEO will not replace SEO — they will increasingly work together as complementary strategies. While SEO focuses on strategies to drive organic website traffic, AEO optimizes for AI-generated answers that may not always lead to clicks. The relationship is symbiotic — strong SEO fuels AEO success since AI systems favor content from trusted domains with solid organic rankings and authority. What is the difference between SEO, AEO, and GEO? SEO, AEO, and GEO aren't three separate, competing practices. SEO, together with Agentic Search Optimization (ASO), is the umbrella discipline for earning visibility everywhere people search. And AEO and GEO are two lenses within SEO and ASO. AEO and GEO target different layers of how AI systems find and use your content. Here's how AEO and GEO differ: AEO (answer engine optimization) focuses on the retrieval and citation layer — getting your existing content pulled into direct AI-generated answers and featured snippets in real time, as a user asks a question GEO (generative engine optimization) focuses on the model layer — how a brand appears in what an AI model already knows from its training data, independent of any single search or retrieval moment Both AEO and GEO roll up under SEO and ASO because the underlying inputs — authority, structure, relevance, and technical health — are the same ones that get a page ranked, retrieved, and cited in the first place. Can you optimize one page for both SEO and AEO? Yes, you can — and should — optimize one page for both SEO and AEO, by: Structuring content logically with proper headings Enriching it with original research and expert insights Using clear entities for topic relevance Keeping information current and comprehensive What tools can you use for SEO and AEO? text: Quick answer SEO (search engine optimization) earns rankings and clicks in search results. AEO (answer engine optimization) earns mentions and citations inside AI-generated answers from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Google's AI Overviews and AI Mode. They share a foundation (crawlable, authoritative, well-structured content), but AEO is judged per passage rather than per page, counts brand mentions as well as links, and is measured as a rate across repeated AI runs rather than a fixed position. You need both: SEO gets you retrieved, AEO gets you quoted. Written October 2026. Measure is an AI search visibility platform, so we have a view; where we cite third-party data, the source is linked. Key takeaways SEO optimizes a page to rank for a keyword. AEO optimizes passages, facts and your brand's off-site footprint so an AI engine uses them when it writes an answer. Most of the work overlaps: crawlability, authority, clear structure, original content and freshness help both. The differences are in the last mile. AEO adds four things SEO rarely tracks: unlinked brand mentions, passage-level extractability, AI crawler access beyond Googlebot, and visibility measured across many sampled answers. Report both on one scorecard: rankings and organic clicks next to mention rate, citation rate, AI share of voice and AI referral traffic. AEO vs SEO at a glance The short version: SEO decides whether your page is shown. AEO decides whether an AI engine uses what is on the page, or what other sites say about you, when it writes the answer. Here is how the two compare on the dimensions that change how you work. SEO AEO Goal Rank pages in search results and win clicks Be mentioned, recommended or cited in AI answers Where it shows up Google and Bing results, featured snippets, PAA, local pack ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, AI Overviews, AI Mode Unit that competes The page The passage, the fact, and the brand Input from the user Keywords, often 2 to 5 words Prompts, often full sentences with constraints How the engine searches One query, one ranked list Many sub-queries per prompt (query fan-out) Main signals Relevance, links, content quality, page experience Relevance per sub-query, authority, extractability, mentions across trusted sources Off-site signal Backlinks Backlinks plus unlinked mentions, reviews, forums, directories Crawlers that matter Googlebot, Bingbot Those plus OAI-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot and others Visibility is A position, fairly stable day to day A probability, varies run to run What success looks like Rankings, impressions, organic clicks Mention rate, citation rate, AI share of voice, AI referrals Click behaviour Click is the point Many answers end without a click; influence counts Time to effect Weeks to months Days for retrieval-based engines, longer for model memory Main tools Rank trackers, Search Console, crawlers, keyword tools AI visibility trackers, citation source reports, Search Console AI report, GA4 AI channel Biggest risk of ignoring it No organic traffic AI recommends competitors and describes you with someone else's facts AEO vs SEO compared on 14 dimensions, October 2026. What is SEO? SEO (search engine optimization) is the practice of making web pages rank higher in search engines such as Google and Bing, so more people find and click them. It covers three areas: technical SEO (making pages crawlable, indexable and fast), on-page SEO (matching content, titles and structure to what searchers want) and off-page SEO (earning links and reputation from other sites). The unit of competition in SEO is the page, and the outcome is a position on a results page. Even with AI features layered on top, the core loop has not changed: Google crawls a page, indexes it, ranks it against other pages for a query, and the searcher decides whether to click. What is AEO? AEO (answer engine optimization) is the practice of getting your brand and your content mentioned, recommended and cited inside AI-generated answers. An answer engine is any system that responds to a question with a written answer instead of a list of links: ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, and Google's own AI Overviews and AI Mode. For example, if you sell accounting software for agencies, AEO is the work that makes your product appear when someone asks ChatGPT "what's the best accounting software for a small creative agency?", with accurate pricing and a link to your site. Our AEO glossary entry has the short definition. AEO, GEO, LLMO, AI SEO: one practice, several names You will see the same work called generative engine optimization (GEO), LLM optimization (LLMO), AI search optimization or AI SEO. We treat these as interchangeable, and so do most practitioners. Some vendors draw a line, using AEO for getting retrieved and cited in live answers and GEO for shaping what a model already knows from training data. That distinction is real (see model memory below), but the tactics overlap so much that splitting the discipline in two adds little. The fuller definition lives in our GEO entry . How a page wins in SEO vs in AEO The clearest way to see the difference is to put the two pipelines next to each other. The first three steps of AEO depend on SEO. The last three are where AEO becomes its own discipline. SEO ends in a click on a ranked page. AEO ends in a mention or citation inside a written answer. Prompt. The user asks a full question, often with constraints ("for a team of 15", "under $50", "that integrates with HubSpot"). Fan-out. The engine splits the prompt into several searches, one per intent. This is query fan-out , and it is why a single prompt can draw on a dozen different pages. Retrieve. Each sub-query is run against a search index: Google's for AI Overviews, AI Mode and Gemini, Bing and other providers for ChatGPT and Copilot, and each engine's own crawl. This is the step SEO controls. A page that is not indexed or ranks nowhere is never seen. Score passages. Retrieved pages are split into passages and ranked for how well each one answers each sub-query. A page that ranks seventh can supply the best passage. Write the answer. The model writes from the top passages and from what it already knows. Cite or mention. Some sources get a visible citation and link. Others shape the wording without being cited. Brands can be mentioned with no link at all. The one-line summary SEO gets your page retrieved. AEO gets your passage chosen and your brand named. Where AEO and SEO overlap Most of what makes a site good for SEO also makes it good for AEO. That is the most important practical point in this whole comparison, because it means you are not starting a second program from scratch. Crawlability and indexation. If a page is blocked, slow to render or not indexed, it can neither rank nor be retrieved. Authority. Engines of both kinds lean on domains that other trusted sites reference. Strong sites get retrieved more often, which gives their passages more chances to be used. Clear structure. Descriptive headings, short paragraphs, lists and tables help Google generate snippets and help answer engines extract passages. Original, experience-based content. First-hand data, tests and expert views are what both Google's helpful content systems and answer engines prefer over rewritten summaries. Freshness. Current prices, dates and examples help in both, and matter even more when an engine adds the current year to its sub-queries. Structured data. Schema markup clarifies entities and facts for search features and for AI systems that read the page. Google itself says there is nothing extra you have to do to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode beyond following its normal search guidance. That is true as far as it goes: the entry ticket is SEO. What it doesn't cover is everything that happens after retrieval, and the engines Google doesn't run. 8 ways AEO differs from SEO 1. Passages compete, not pages In SEO, the whole page is ranked. In AEO, a single paragraph, table row or list item can be lifted and used, and the rest of the page doesn't matter for that sub-query. A section that buries its answer in the fourth sentence, or relies on "it" and "this" to refer back to earlier context, is hard to extract. Lead each section with a complete, standalone answer. 2. Mentions count, not just links SEO rewards backlinks. Answer engines also read what other pages say about you in plain text. An unlinked line in a Reddit thread, a review on G2 or a mention in an industry roundup can shape whether, and how, a model describes your brand. That makes digital PR, reviews and community presence part of AEO in a way they were only indirectly part of SEO. 3. Prompts, not keywords People type short keywords into Google and full questions into ChatGPT. A prompt carries constraints (team size, budget, location, integration) that a keyword never does. AEO research therefore starts from real buyer questions, gathered from sales calls, support tickets and community threads, and tracks those prompts directly. Keywords still name your pages; prompts decide what the pages must answer. 4. A probability, not a position Run the same prompt ten times and you get different answers, different sources and sometimes different recommended brands. AI visibility is a rate: the share of runs in which you are mentioned or cited. That is why a screenshot of one answer proves very little, and why AEO tracking samples each prompt repeatedly over time. See our explainer on AI share of voice for how that rate is compared against competitors. 5. Influence without the click In SEO, a ranking that earns no clicks is worth little. In AEO, a buyer can read an answer that recommends you, never click, and then search your brand name or type your URL a week later. Some of that value shows up as branded search or direct traffic, not as an AI referral. The click data is still worth having: independent studies of AI referrals generally find them small in volume and, for considered purchases, converting at or above organic search. −58% Top-result CTR where an AI Overview shows (Ahrefs, Feb 2026) +35% More organic clicks for brands cited in the AI Overview (Seer) 11.4% AI referral conversion rate vs 5.3% organic (Similarweb, Jun 2025) The Seer figure is the one to remember for this comparison: being cited inside the AI Overview recovers part of the click loss that the AI Overview causes. AEO is partly a defence of SEO traffic. Sources and grading are in our AI search statistics reference. 6. Many engines and indexes, not one SEO is mostly Google, plus Bing. AEO covers at least five major assistants, each with its own retrieval stack and crawler. ChatGPT and Copilot draw heavily on Bing-based and other providers' results; Perplexity runs its own crawl; Claude uses a web search provider. A site that ranks well on Google but blocks OAI-SearchBot or PerplexityBot, or that Bing barely indexes, can be invisible in those engines. Our free AI crawler checker shows which bots your robots.txt allows. 7. Third-party pages carry more weight For "best X", "X vs Y" and "is X worth it" prompts, answer engines often retrieve review sites, listicles, forums and video transcripts rather than vendor pages. In SEO you can rank your own comparison page; in AEO you also need to be present, and described accurately, on the pages the engines actually cite. A citation source report tells you which domains those are for your prompts. 8. The model's memory is a second layer SEO has one layer: the live index. Answer engines have two. Besides what they retrieve, models answer from what they learned in training, which is months old and built from the wider web. If your brand was barely discussed when the model was trained, it may describe your category without you, or with stale facts, even when no search is run. You influence this layer slowly, through consistent, widely repeated information about your brand across many sources. Retrieval is where most of the short-term gains are. Does ranking on Google get you cited by AI? Partly. Ranking well helps, because a page has to be retrieved before it can be cited, and strong domains are retrieved more often. But the relationship is loose, for three reasons: Engines retrieve from different indexes. Google's AI features lean on Google's index; ChatGPT and Copilot do not. Overlap between a Google top 10 and the sources an assistant cites varies a lot by engine. Sub-queries are not your keyword. The engine searches for the pieces of the prompt, so the page it cites may rank for a sub-query you never tracked. Passages beat pages. Within a trusted domain, engines often cite a deeper page, a doc or a help article rather than the URL that ranks for the head term. The practical reading: treat SEO as necessary and AEO as the work that turns retrieval into citation. If you rank well and still don't get cited, the gap is usually extractability, missing facts on your pages, or your absence from the third-party pages engines prefer. Tactic SEO impact AEO impact Fix crawling, rendering and indexation High High Allow AI crawlers in robots.txt and your CDN None High Answer-first sections with question headings Medium High Publish real pricing, specs, integrations and limits Medium High Original research and first-hand data High High Earn backlinks from relevant sites High Medium Earn mentions in reviews, roundups and forums Low High Honest comparison and alternatives pages High High Topic clusters with strong internal links High Medium Schema markup (Organization, Product, FAQ, Article) Medium Medium Keep facts current, with visible update dates Medium High Title tag and meta description testing High Low Consistent entity naming across the web Low High Typical impact; your mileage depends on market and site maturity. Create content only you can write Both channels reward information that doesn't exist elsewhere. Publish your own numbers (usage data, survey results, benchmarks), document real tests, and name the people who did the work with short author bios. Original data also earns the backlinks and mentions that feed authority in both channels. State the facts engines look for Answer engines check attributes before they recommend something: price, plans, integrations, limits, setup time, security, support. If your site hides these behind "contact sales" or in images and PDFs, the engine takes them from someone else. Put them in plain HTML text, in tables where possible, with the date they were last checked. Be consistent about who you are Use the same brand name, product names and category description everywhere: your site, your Organization schema, LinkedIn, Crunchbase, G2, press boilerplate. Consistent entity signals help Google's Knowledge Graph and help language models connect your brand to the right category. If your homepage says "revenue intelligence", your G2 profile says "sales analytics" and your press release says "AI forecasting", engines may not realize these describe one product. Work the pages engines actually cite Pull the list of domains AI engines cite for your target prompts. Then work it like a link-building list, but aimed at presence and accuracy: get included in the roundups, keep review profiles complete, answer questions in the communities that show up, and correct wrong facts where you can. This is the single biggest AEO lever that a pure SEO program usually misses. Refresh, don't just re-date Update the substance: new prices, current screenshots, this year's data, removed references to tools that no longer exist. Changing the date without changing the content helps neither Google nor answer engines, and can mislead readers. SEO (search engine optimization) earns rankings and clicks in search results. AEO (answer engine optimization) earns mentions and citations inside AI-generated answers from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude and Google's AI features. SEO competes page by page for a position; AEO competes passage by passage and is measured as a rate across repeated AI answers. Will AEO replace SEO? No. Answer engines retrieve sources from search indexes, so a page has to be crawlable, indexed and trusted before it can be cited. AEO is added on top of SEO: it covers passage extractability, published facts, AI crawler access and third-party mentions. What is the difference between AEO and GEO? Does ranking #1 on Google get you cited in ChatGPT? Not reliably. Good rankings help a page get retrieved, but ChatGPT does not use Google's index, engines search for the sub-questions in a prompt rather than your keyword, and they choose individual passages. Target the keyword in the title and headings for SEO, then open each section with a complete, standalone answer, state facts such as prices and limits in plain text or tables, keep entity names consistent and show when it was last updated. AEO is the practice of optimizing content so it appears as a direct answer in search results. The "answer engine" is any system that responds to a query with a synthesized answer rather than a list of links. Answer engines include: Google AI Overviews . AI-generated summaries at the top of search results Featured snippets . The answer box that appears above organic result #1 Google's People Also Ask . Expandable Q&A sections in search results Voice assistants . Google Assistant, Siri, Alexa answering spoken questions AI search platforms . ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot The goal of AEO is not a #1 ranking. The goal is being the source that the answer engine selects, quotes, or cites when generating its response. Your content becomes the answer itself. What Is SEO? SEO targets the traditional ranked results on search engines. Google indexes pages, evaluates them on relevance and authority, and displays a list of 10 blue links. The user clicks a link, visits the page, and consumes content on your site. SEO operates on established signals: Keywords match user queries to relevant pages Backlinks indicate authority and trust Technical optimization ensures search engines can crawl and index content Content quality satisfies user intent and reduces bounce rates User experience keeps visitors engaged and returning The SEO industry exceeds $80 billion. For most businesses, organic search remains the largest source of website traffic. The fundamentals have not changed in over a decade. What has changed is the surface area where results appear. AEO vs GEO vs AI Overviews: Clearing Up the Confusion Three terms. Overlapping concepts. Different scopes. Here is how they relate. Term What It Targets Scope Origin AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) Featured snippets, voice assistants, answer boxes, AI answers Narrow: single query → direct answer Pre-AI era (featured snippets, voice search) GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, AI Overviews, Copilot Broad: how AI represents your brand across conversations AI era (Princeton 2023 paper) AIO (AI Overview Optimization) Google AI Overviews specifically Narrow: Google's AI-generated summary block Google SGE/AI Overviews rollout (2024-2025) AEO is the oldest term. It emerged when featured snippets and voice search became prominent around 2017-2018. The concept was simple: format your content so Google pulls it as the direct answer. GEO is the broadest term. It covers everything AEO covers plus AI platform optimization, brand entity management, and citation optimization across generative engines . For a deeper comparison, see our GEO vs SEO guide . AIO is the most specific. It targets Google's AI Overview feature exclusively. In practice, most AEO tactics also serve GEO goals. The distinction matters for measurement. AEO tracks whether you win the featured snippet. GEO tracks whether ChatGPT mentions your brand. Both require structured, citable content, but GEO demands stronger third-party brand signals. Why AEO Matters Now: The Data The numbers explain the urgency. The Zero-Click Reality 65% of Google searches end without a click. On mobile, the zero-click rate reaches 77.2%. When an AI Overview appears, the rate jumps to 83%. Traditional SEO assumes users will click your link. A growing majority never do. But zero-click does not mean zero value. Being cited in an AI Overview generates 35% more organic clicks than a non-cited position-1 result. Being the answer builds brand recognition even when the user does not visit your site. The Conversion Paradox AI-referred visitors convert at 12-18% compared to 2.8% for traditional organic. Answer engines extract concise passages. If your answer is buried in paragraph 6, the AI will find a competitor's answer in paragraph 1 instead. Format: State the answer clearly in 1-2 sentences Follow with supporting context and evidence Expand into full detail in the sections below Pages that lead with a direct answer have 2.8 times higher AI citation rates than pages that build to the answer gradually. 2. Use Question-Based Headings Voice queries average 29 words and almost always take a question format. Featured snippets trigger on question-intent queries 65% of the time. Structure your headings as questions. Instead of: "Benefits of Content Marketing" Write: "What Are the Benefits of Content Marketing?" Question headings match the way people speak to voice assistants and type into AI chat interfaces. They also align with Google's People Also Ask format, which feeds both featured snippet selection and AI Overview content. 3. Build FAQ Sections on Every Post Pages with FAQ schema are 3.2 times more likely to appear in Google AI Overviews. FAQ sections provide pre-formatted question-answer pairs that answer engines can extract directly. Every blog post should include 4-6 FAQs at the end. Source questions from: Google's People Also Ask results Reddit and Quora discussions Related searches at the bottom of SERPs Customer questions your sales team hears regularly 4. Use HTML Tables for Comparisons Answer engines prefer HTML tables over images for data comparison. A table comparing "AEO vs SEO" in HTML is machine-readable. The same comparison as a PNG image is invisible to AI extraction. Use tables for: Feature comparisons Pricing breakdowns Pros and cons Statistics summaries Timeline comparisons 5. Add Statistics With Source Citations The Princeton GEO study proved that adding statistics with source citations increases AI visibility by 33%. Answer engines trust content that cites verifiable data. Unsourced claims get deprioritized. Every major claim in your content should link to a credible source. Prioritize .edu, .gov, and established industry publications (Ahrefs, Semrush, HubSpot, Moz). 6. Optimize for Voice Search Specifically Voice search answers pull from different content than text search results. Google Home, Siri, and Alexa share only 1% answer overlap for identical queries. Each voice assistant draws from different data sources. For Google Assistant: Optimize Google Business Profile, use structured data, win featured snippets. For Siri: Ensure Apple Maps listing is complete and consistent. For Alexa: Optimize for Bing and Amazon ecosystem presence. Voice search pages average 2,312 words. Long-form, authoritative content with a clear answer in the opening section performs best across all voice platforms. 7. Build Entity Clarity Answer engines identify content by entities (people, businesses, products, topics) not just keywords. Make your brand entity consistent and clear across the web. ✓ Consistent business name, description, and category across all platforms ✓ Wikipedia or Wikidata presence (if eligible) ✓ Consistent author bios with credentials on all published content ✓ Organization schema on your homepage ✓ Brand mentions on Reddit, industry forums, and review platforms ✓ Active Google Business Profile with regular posts and reviews 3,500+ blogs published. text: Key Takeaways Semrush's AI Overviews study of 10M+ keywords found AI Overviews on 6.49% of queries in January 2025 and 15.69% by November, after peaking at 24.61% in July. AEO and SEO share the same technical foundation, crawlability, page speed, and E-E-A-T signals, meaning teams that skip foundational SEO will see limited gains from AEO tactics alone. SEO is tracked by rankings and organic clicks, while AEO is measured by snippet capture, answer impressions and how often AI responses cite your brand. One renewable energy client grew organic traffic 900% in 10 months by fixing technical SEO first and adding answer-ready content, with $1.1 million in SEO-attributed revenue. Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) is the practice of structuring content so that AI-driven search features (Google's AI Overviews, featured snippets, and voice assistants) select it as the direct answer to a query. Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is the broader discipline of earning rankings and organic clicks across the full results page. The two are related, not rival: AEO builds on the same technical and authority foundations as SEO, but it optimizes for a different win condition. The practical question most marketing teams face is not which one replaces the other, but how much of their content program should shift toward AEO-specific tactics, and whether the two can run in parallel without doubling the workload. That question is worth answering carefully, because the differences in workflow, KPIs, and tooling are real even if the underlying discipline is shared. Short on time to work through this yourself? Find out more about our AEO agency services . Quick Verdict AEO vs SEO is not a binary choice. AEO is best understood as a layer on top of SEO, requiring the same crawlable site, strong E-E-A-T signals, and quality content, but adding answer-first structure, schema markup, and a different measurement model. If your SEO foundation is weak, AEO tactics will underperform. If your SEO foundation is solid, adding AEO-specific practices is a logical next step, not a separate program. How the Two Disciplines Differ in Practice The clearest way to separate AEO vs SEO is by their primary win condition. SEO aims to rank a URL as high as possible in the list of results so users click through to the page. AEO aims to get content extracted and displayed directly in the results interface: a featured snippet, a People Also Ask box, or an AI Overview. The goal is for the brand to earn visibility even when the user does not click. This difference changes how content is written. SEO content is typically structured to cover a topic comprehensively, building topical authority across a cluster of pages. According to Google's structured data documentation , structured data helps Google understand a page and can make it eligible for rich results, while Google's guidance on AI features says no special markup is needed to appear in AI Overviews. AEO content prioritizes a concise, quotable answer in the opening paragraph, followed by supporting detail, which is the reverse of a traditional long-form SEO structure. Keyword strategy also diverges. SEO focuses on head and mid-tail keywords mapped to user intent and search volume. AEO targets the natural-language questions those keywords imply: the full question a user might type or speak, rather than the compressed phrase. A keyword like "solar panel installation cost" becomes the AEO question "How much does it cost to have solar panels installed?" Both are worth targeting; they just require different content treatments on the same or related pages. AEO vs SEO KPIs and What You Actually Track The measurement gap between the two disciplines is where most teams get stuck. SEO KPIs are well-established: organic sessions, keyword rankings, click-through rate, and conversion rate from organic traffic. These are available in Google Search Console, any rank-tracking platform, and your analytics stack. The feedback loop is fast enough that you can see ranking movement within weeks of publishing or updating a page. AEO KPIs are less standardized. The core metrics are snippet capture rate (what percentage of target questions your content answers visibly in the SERP), featured answer impressions in Search Console, and, for AI Overview and LLM citation tracking, brand mention frequency in AI-generated responses. That last metric requires dedicated tooling; it is not available natively in Search Console. Tools built for this tracking are covered in our LLM visibility tracking overview . AI Overviews are now common enough to measure: in Semrush's AI Overviews study of more than 10 million keywords, they appeared on 6.49% of queries in January 2025, peaked at 24.61% in July and were at 15.69% in November. According to Semrush data reported by Search Engine Land , pages that appear in AI Overviews do not always see a corresponding increase in organic clicks, confirming that impression-based metrics need to sit alongside, not replace, traffic-based ones. This is one of the more uncomfortable truths about AEO: brand visibility and site traffic can move in opposite directions, at least in the short term. What AEO and SEO Actually Share The overlap between the two disciplines is larger than most introductory content acknowledges. Both require a technically sound site: fast load times, clean crawlability, mobile rendering, and no critical indexing errors. Before investing in AEO-specific content tactics, it is worth running a technical and content audit to confirm the foundation is solid, because schema markup on a slow or poorly structured site delivers far less lift than on a well-optimized one. E-E-A-T (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness) matters equally to both. Google's AI systems draw on the same quality signals as its traditional ranking algorithm when deciding which sources to surface in AI Overviews. A site that lacks author credentials, thin content, or weak backlink authority will struggle to earn AEO placements regardless of how well the content is structured for answers. Backlinks remain relevant to AEO. AI Overview sourcing favors content from sites that have established topical authority and strong inbound link profiles. The underlying logic is the same as traditional SEO: links signal trust, and trust influences which content gets surfaced. This is covered in more detail in our article on why link building matters for search authority . Tools and Workflow: Where the Differences Show Up Daily An SEO workflow typically centers on a rank tracker, a keyword research tool, a site audit platform, and a backlink database. The cycle is monthly: audit, prioritize, publish or update, track rankings, repeat. Most of this workflow applies directly to AEO, with two additions: schema implementation and question-based content auditing. Schema markup is useful AEO groundwork, but not a shortcut. Google limited FAQ rich results to well-known government and health sites in 2023 and retired HowTo rich results, and its guidance on AI features says no special markup is needed to appear in AI Overviews. Structured data that accurately describes the page still helps Google understand it, and it costs a few hours per template rather than new content, which makes it a sensible early step for teams running pure SEO programs. Question-based content auditing means reviewing your existing content library for pages that answer specific questions but bury the answer below an introduction, a definition section, or multiple paragraphs of context. Moving the direct answer to the first sentence or two of a section, before any supporting detail, is the formatting change most likely to win the snippet. This is a workflow step, not a tool, but it requires someone to systematically audit pages rather than waiting for new content briefs. For teams that want dedicated AEO tooling, the landscape is covered in our roundup of AEO tools for 2026 . The short version: most established SEO platforms have added some answer-tracking features, but dedicated AEO tools offer more granular question-gap analysis and snippet monitoring. For informational queries ("what size solar panel do I need?" or "how does heat pump installation work?"), AEO tactics apply directly and product pages benefit from FAQ schema, structured specifications, and direct-answer copy. For transactional queries, traditional SEO still dominates because AI Overviews are less common on high-commercial-intent searches, and Google routes those queries to Shopping results and paid listings instead. For B2B content programs, AEO has the clearest ROI at the top of the funnel. Decision-makers using AI search to research categories and shortlist vendors represent a growing share of early-stage demand. Getting your content cited in those AI-generated summaries builds brand authority before a prospect ever visits your site, a form of visibility that traditional SEO rankings cannot replicate. This is especially relevant for businesses in competitive or technical categories where buyers use AI tools to get oriented before engaging with vendors. What Combined SEO and AEO Looks Like in Practice One of our clients, a renewable energy business in the UK, illustrates what a technically grounded, answer-optimized content program can produce. They entered the market with no organic presence, no in-house SEO resource, and a heavy dependence on paid ads. We migrated and consolidated their acquired domains (redirecting over 600 URLs without losing link equity), built service and local landing pages structured around buyer intent, added schema markup, and launched a backlink acquisition program to close the authority gap against established competitors. The result over 10 months: 900% organic traffic growth, 121% growth in referring domains, and $1.1 million in revenue attributed to SEO. You can read the full case study for the sequencing detail. The point relevant here is that none of the AEO-specific work (structured data, answer-first page formatting) would have delivered at that scale without the technical and authority foundation being rebuilt first. Which One to Prioritize: Specific Scenarios Start with SEO if: your site has significant technical debt (crawl errors, slow load times, thin content), your domain authority is low relative to competitors, or you have no existing keyword rankings to build on. AEO tactics layered onto a weak technical foundation produce marginal gains at best. Add AEO if: you already rank on page one for a cluster of informational queries but your click-through rate is declining, you operate in a category where AI Overviews are common (health, finance, home services, B2B SaaS), or your content team is already producing comprehensive topic coverage and needs a formatting and schema layer rather than net-new content. Run both in parallel if: you have a mature SEO program, an established content calendar, and the ability to add schema implementation and question-based content auditing to your existing workflow without creating separate workstreams. The two disciplines share enough infrastructure that parallel operation is achievable for most teams without doubling headcount or budget. Prioritize AEO over SEO if: you are in a category where your target audience is visibly shifting to AI-first research behavior, your brand needs citation-level awareness rather than click-through traffic, or your competitors have strong rankings but weak structured data coverage, which creates a gap you can close quickly. If you're asking what is SEO vs GEO vs AEO and how they all fit together, the broader framework is covered in our SEO, GEO, and AEO comparison . Your First Three Decisions This Week 1. Audit your top 10 informational pages for answer-first formatting. Open each page and check whether the first 60 words of each major section contain a direct, quotable answer to the question implied by the heading. If they do not, that is your editing queue, and no new content is required. 2. Check structured data in Google Search Console. Open the Enhancements section to see which structured data types Google detects on your pages and any errors. Fix errors on your top informational pages first, and make sure each type describes what the page actually shows. Google Search Console is free and the report takes under five minutes to read. 3. Decide whether your measurement stack can track snippet capture rate. Pull your Search Console data filtered to question-format queries (queries starting with "how," "what," "why," "when"). Look at the Average Position and CTR columns. Pages ranking in positions 1 to 3 with below-average CTR are likely losing clicks to featured snippets or AI Overviews that are not yours — that is the AEO gap to close first. FAQ What is the difference between AEO and SEO? SEO (Search Engine Optimization) focuses on earning high rankings in the organic search results list so users click through to your website. AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) focuses on structuring content so that AI-driven features (featured snippets, AI Overviews, voice assistants) extract and display your answer directly in the search interface. AEO requires the same technical and authority foundations as SEO, but adds answer-first content formatting and schema markup as specific tactics. Is SEO replaced by AI or by AEO? No. AI search features change the win conditions for visibility, but the underlying signals (domain authority, content quality, crawlability, E-E-A-T) remain the same. AEO is an extension of SEO, not a replacement. Sites that perform well in traditional rankings tend to perform well in AI-generated answers too, because both systems draw on the same trust signals. The practical change is that click-through rates from ranked positions are declining on informational queries, which makes impression-based AEO metrics increasingly important alongside traffic-based SEO metrics. Do I need AEO if I already do SEO? It depends on your query mix. If a significant share of your target keywords are informational (how-to, what-is, comparison queries) and you are already ranking well but seeing declining click volume, AEO-specific tactics (answer-first formatting, FAQ schema, question-gap analysis) are a logical next layer. If your content program is primarily transactional or your SEO foundation has significant technical gaps, fixing those gaps first will generate more return than adding AEO tactics to a weak base. text: What is Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)? By Despina Gavoyannis Senior SEO Specialist at Ahrefs Contributors Ryan Law August 28, 2025 AEO Guide 01 What Is Answer Engine Optimization (AEO)? What is answer engine optimization? AEO vs SEO Why is AEO important? How to get started with AEO How long does answer engine optimization take? Future trends in AEO 02 How Answer Engines Work 03 How to Track AI Visibility 04 How to Choose the Best Prompts to Track 05 How to Optimize Content for Answer Engines 06 How to Monitor and Win Brand Mentions in AI Answers 07 How to Optimize Your Website for Answer Engines 08 How to Spot and Fix Mistakes in AI Answers Search is changing. People are no longer just “Googling it.” Increasingly, they’re asking AI systems for answers and getting them instantly without having to click and sift through different websites. SEO is still essential for brands to show up in these answers, but visibility now depends on more than rankings. What matters is whether your brand and content are trusted and structured enough to be mentioned (your brand discussed in AI answers) or cited (your pages linked to in AI answers). This is where answer engine optimization, or AEO, comes in. It builds on SEO fundamentals and adapts them for AI search, helping your brand become the answer wherever people are asking. Keep learning on YouTube Part 1 What is answer engine optimization? Answer engine optimization (AEO) is the practice of making your content visible and useful to AI systems that deliver direct answers, whether that’s Google’s AI Overviews, voice assistants, or LLMs like ChatGPT and Claude. Unlike traditional SEO, which focuses on ranking web pages in search results, AEO is about being mentioned and cited directly in the answers generated by AI search platforms. That requires content to be clear, structured, and trustworthy so that answer engines can easily extract and present it. Part 2 AEO vs SEO AEO doesn’t replace SEO; it complements it. Both share the goal of making content discoverable, but they differ in how that content reaches people. SEO is still about ranking pages in organic search results. However, AEO is specifically about being cited or mentioned in AI answers, where there may not even be a list of links to click. AEO SEO Primary goal Surface your brand and content inside AI-generated answers. Rank pages in search results. Content focus Concise, declarative answers that AI can easily summarize. Long-form, comprehensive pages that send ranking signals. Query targeting Question-based and informational queries, often “1 of 1” searches, unique to LLMs. Broad, high-volume queries, including local and transactional ones. Technical elements Avoid JavaScript reliance, use speakable and FAQ schema, and provide clean datasets and answers AI can extract directly. Optimize on-page elements like meta tags, headings, and internal links. Measurement Track citations and mentions in AI Overviews, LLM responses, and chatbot conversations. Track webpage rankings, clicks, and impressions. User journey Often delivers brand exposure without a click (zero-click visibility). Encourages clicks to your site for deeper engagement. AEO is still grounded in SEO fundamentals. You need crawlable, optimized content to be seen in the first place. But once the basics are covered, the focus shifts from ranking a page to packaging information in a way AI can trust and reuse. Part 3 Why is AEO important? The way people consume information is changing. Instead of clicking through multiple sites, they expect direct answers wherever they search. This shift has several major implications for brands: Zero-click searches are becoming the norm. AI-generated answers often resolve a query on the spot. Even if users never visit your site, appearing in the cited answer can still build authority and brand recognition through search. Organic traffic is under pressure. Traditional rankings still matter, but clicks are no longer guaranteed . Visibility inside AI responses is now as critical as visibility in traditional search result pages. Business impact goes beyond SEO. When fewer visitors reach your website, the effects ripple through sales, product, and customer success teams. Therefore, protecting brand presence in AI answers ensures customers continue to encounter your expertise, even off-site. AI is shaping new user habits. Voice-ready answers and conversational interactions are still early, but they’re growing quickly. As AI assistants become part of everyday work and personal life, people will rely on them as default gateways to information. In short, search experiences are moving from links to answers . Brands that adapt with AEO can maintain visibility, authority, and customer trust in a landscape where traffic alone is no longer the only measure of success. Part 4 How to get started with AEO Getting started with AEO means shifting your mindset from ranking pages to being mentioned and cited. That requires targeting the right questions, structuring content in a way answer engines can easily access, and strengthening the authority signals that make your brand a trustworthy source. The steps below outline a practical AEO process you can follow to build consistent visibility in AI-powered search results. We’ll cover each of these in more detail in subsequent chapters. Step 1: Start tracking your AI visibility If you have an existing brand, start by discovering what answer engines like ChatGPT are already saying about it, using an AI visibility tool like Ahrefs’ Brand Radar . You can check this manually at a small scale, but it’s an expensive process: every answer engine, from ChatGPT to AI Mode to Claude, will say something different about your brand. In the AI responses tab of Brand Radar, you can quickly see what different AI search platforms say about your brand: You can also compare it to what they say about competitors and how much coverage you have in your market or niche. Check out the AI answers provided for common queries. They’ll look like this: Look for patterns in what AI answers say about you, especially when they get things wrong or when your branding is inconsistent. It helps to list these queries and the sources cited so you can work on overcoming the misinformation and brand inconsistencies. Step 2: Choose the right prompts to track Every business has a handful of business-critical topics for which they want excellent visibility. As part of your answer engine optimization process, you can identify these topics, create prompts based on them, and monitor if and how your brand appears in the responses to these prompts. This is known as prompt tracking. Here’s what it looks like in Brand Radar: If you’re wondering which prompts you should track, we recommend a few different types: Non-branded discovery prompts : The “best X for Y” questions your buyers ask before they know you exist. Sourced from People Also Ask, question keywords, and forum threads, these show whether you’re in the consideration set at all. Example: What’s the best SEO tool for a small in-house marketing team? Brand accuracy prompts : Questions specifically about you, covering pricing, features, complaints, and competitive positioning. The point is checking whether what AI says matches reality, since inaccuracies here directly cost deals. Example: Does Ahrefs let you track custom AI prompts? Conversational versions of your money keywords : Take the terms driving traffic to your highest-converting pages and rewrite them as natural language. This anchors your tracking to topics with proven commercial value. Example: “free keyword generator” becomes Where can I generate keyword ideas without paying for a subscription? Competitor gap prompts : Queries where rivals get mentioned and you don’t. These double as a content audit, since absence usually means you have no relevant page. Example: Which tools show you which sites link to my competitors but not to me? Topics you already appear in : The themes AI currently associates with your brand. Worth tracking because these are the easiest positions to lose and the cheapest to defend. Example: How do I check a website’s domain rating? If you’re unsure, start by prioritizing queries around high-value topics. You can always expand your prompt tracking later. Step 3: Fix incorrect information about your brand in AI answers If AI answers include incorrect details about your brand, it usually comes down to: Too little information on your website Inconsistent assets like logos, taglines, or messaging Misrepresentation by third-party content AI pulling from unreliable sources Start by reviewing the queries where errors appear. Note what’s wrong and which sources were cited. For brand-specific details (like your name, tagline, or mission statement), check your site and social profiles for consistency first. You can follow our brand SEO process to do this. You may need to close content gaps on your website to correct more general misinformation about your brand. For example, the query “what does Ahrefs stand for” produces a passable answer in Google’s AI Overviews, but it’s not a direct answer to the question. It’s likely because there is no content on the website answering this exact question. So, if we wanted to make the answer more accurate, we could add a short FAQ to the page that’s cited in the AI response already. Something like: What does Ahrefs stand for? Ahrefs stands for “a href,” the HTML tag that creates hyperlinks in code. The name reflects the company’s origins in backlink analysis and highlights its focus on links, search visibility, and building tools that help websites improve SEO performance. If your site has no information on a query, publish a new page or section to fill the gap. Here’s a helpful workflow for this: If content exists but AI still incorrectly cites other sources, consider updating your content on third-party sites like G2, YouTube, Google Business, and more. You can also try outreach. Contact the cited authors and offer updated, accurate information to ensure your brand is represented correctly. It’s slower, but worthwhile if misinformation risks confusing or losing clients. Step 4: Create and optimize content to rank in AI search Once you know which topics you’re already visible for, the next step is finding the ones you’re missing. Brand Radar’s Overview tab compares your AI visibility against your competitors across mentions, impressions, and AI Share of Voice, broken down by platform. Click into any platform and you can read the actual AI responses behind those numbers, filtered three ways: Only brand (responses mentioning just you), With others (responses mentioning you alongside competitors), and Others only . That last report is the one that matters here. It surfaces every query where AI answers the question, recommends your competitors, and leaves you out entirely. Each of those queries is a topic gap. You already know AI answers questions on the subject and that your competitors are earning the mentions, so the path to closing the gap is straightforward: work down the list, decide which conversations you want to be part of, and create content on the topics worth winning. Once you’ve identified the right queries, the next step is structuring your content so answer engines can easily lift and reuse it. Rank in traditional search first : 88% of ChatGPT’s cited URLs come from its general search index, so a page that can’t be found conventionally never enters the running. Build clusters, not single pages : Prompts get broken into shorter fan-out queries during retrieval, and those queries are probabilistic, so you can’t target one reliably. Look at many in aggregate and cover the recurring themes. Write the formats AI commonly cites : Blog lists dominate ChatGPT’s sources at 43.83%, but comparison pages, original research, definitions, and free tools all answer a question completely and can be verified. Refresh pages that already earn citations : AI-cited URLs are 25.7% fresher than organic results on average, and pages with a proven citation record are the highest-leverage ones to update. Only refresh when something has meaningfully changed. Structure passages so they can be mentioned and cited : 44.2% of citations come from the first 30% of a page, so lead with the answer, write declarative and specific sentences a model can quote verbatim, and repeat your core takeaway across the intro, body, and conclusion. Prioritize information gain. Go beyond surface-level definitions. Provide unique insights, context, or data that make your content more valuable and more likely to be chosen for AI answers over generic alternatives. If you’ve already been structuring your content following SEO best practices , there won’t be much you need to change in your workflow here. If your content is written clearly, structured logically, and provides genuine information gain, you stand the best possible chance of being retrieved by answer engines. Step 5: Build brand mentions Answer engines don’t just look at what’s on your website. They also weigh how the wider web perceives your brand. If you want AI systems to mention your brand or cite your content, you need to demonstrate authority within and beyond your own website. You can strengthen these signals by focusing on: Backlinks and citations: Earn links from reputable domains in your niche, and analyze which sites are most frequently mentioned and cited so you can target them directly. Co-mentions with trusted entities: Aim to have your brand mentioned alongside well-known names or organizations. LLMs can interpret these associations as signals of credibility. Third-party platforms: Keep your information consistent across directories, review sites, and industry publications. These external data points often feed into AI training sets. Taken together, these signals expand your authority footprint beyond your own website. The stronger your presence across the wider web, the more likely answer engines are to recognize and cite your brand. An easy way to earn more relevant links and mentions is to find pages that are frequently cited in AI answers. If you want to build more links and mentions in resources that are frequently cited in AI responses, check out the Cited domains and Cited pages reports in Brand Radar: You can check these out for competitors to find publications that mention them and are likely to also mention you. You can also try it out for websites that frequently write about your core topic. You’ll get a list of websites or pages frequently appearing in AI answers. AI search platforms often visit these pages and summarize their content. Showing up here will reasonably quickly expose your brand to more AI search platforms and earn you more mentions in the answers they generate. Step 6: Implement technical AEO strategies
